articles.title: Food Safety officials conduct State-wide inspection at 45 packaged drinking water units; notices issued to 24
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Food Safety and Drug Administration Department conducted a special State-wide inspection of 45 packaged drinking water units on Thursday.

Several violations, including unhygienic conditions, absence of medical fitness certificates for staff, missing licences from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), labelling defects and failure to produce pest control certificates, were found during the inspection.
As many as 32 water samples have been sent to government food laboratories for testing, while notices have been issued to 24 units for the violations.
Officials of the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department during a special State-wide inspection at packaged drinking water units on Thursday. | Photo Credit: SUDHAKARA JAIN
Misbranded packaged drinking water was seized from units in Mysuru and Davangere. A unit at Mulbagal in Kolar district was shut down due to unhygienic conditions.
Health Minister U.T. Khader has advised consumers to verify the FSSAI licence number, ISI mark, manufacturing date and integrity of the seal before purchasing packaged drinking water.
He also urged the public to report irregularities by scanning the QR code provided for lodging complaints.

articles.title: Three missing fishermen rescued
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Three fishermen from Chollangipeta in Tallarevu mandal in Kakinada district, who went missing after their boat capsized at sea on Tuesday, were rescued by rescue teams.
After their boat capsized, the three managed to swim to Hope Island where they got stranded among the vegetation.
Upon receiving information about the incident, the Fisheries Department, the Real-Time Governance Society (RTGS), and disaster management agencies immediately launched a search and rescue operation.
Using 10 boats, the teams located the fishermen on Thursday and brought them safely back to the shore.

Officials said that such incidents occur when warnings issued to avoid venturing out to sea for fishing due severe weather conditions are ignored. Officials urged fishermen to strictly follow government warnings for their own safety.

articles.title: Power sector suffers ₹500-crore damage due to Cyclone Arnab, says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar on Thursday said that Cyclone Arnab caused an estimated ₹500 crore damage to the power sector and that the government has intensified emergency repairs to the damaged infrastructure, with special focus on Palakollu, Bhimavaram and Narsapur, which bore the brunt of the extreme weather event.

Inspecting the cyclone-hit areas in Bhimavaram on Thursday, Mr. Ravi Kumar said a comprehensive assessment would provide a clearer picture of the true extent of the damages, and that around 1,700 personnel were engaged in the restoration works, with an additional 500 employees being mobilised from the three DISCOMs. Another 500 electricity employees from Telangana joined the operations.

The Minister said the government was ensuring that there was no shortage of manpower, funds or equipment for the restoration efforts and that officials were directed to replace damaged electricity poles, repair snapped conductors, and restore damaged transformers on a priority basis.

articles.title: Fishing boat catches fire near Feroke
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A fishing boat docked beneath the old Feroke bridge caught fire early on Thursday (October 29, 2026) morning, triggering safety concerns among residents. The incident, which occurred when workers were away from the spot, reportedly originated in the boat’s engine and fuel tank.

According to the initial assessment by rescue squads, the blaze broke out in the engine section before spreading to other parts rapidly. Prompt response from emergency personnel helped avert a major disaster. Two officers waded into the river with ropes, swam to the boat, secured it safely, and assisted teams in pulling the vessel closer to the bank.

Fire and rescue services personnel subsequently pumped water to fully extinguish the flames. A rescue officer said a technical malfunction in the boat’s engine caused the fire. He added that further investigations were on to determine the exact cause of the fire.

articles.title: Court directive to add to Kochi Corporation’s Brahmapuram biomining costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kochi Corporation will have to biomine an additional 1.26 lakh tonnes of scientifically capped legacy waste, further adding to its financial burden.

This follows a direction issued by Kerala High Court judges P. Gopinath and Bechu Kurian Thomas during a visit to the Brahmapuram waste treatment plant last month, asking the civic body to include the scientifically capped legacy waste in the biomining process as well. The High Court has been closely monitoring activities at Brahmapuram since a major fire broke out in heaps of plastic waste in 2023 and continued for nearly a fortnight.

Earlier this year, the National Institute of Technology-Calicut (NIT-C) submitted a report to the Corporation estimating the total remaining legacy waste at 3.22 lakh metric tonnes, including the scientifically capped waste. The Corporation had decided not to disturb the capped waste and instead carry out biomining of the remaining 1.96 lakh tonnes at a negotiated rate of ₹1,672 per metric tonne, amounting to ₹37 crore. However, the cost may now have to be recalculated following the directive to include the capped waste as well.

“We will take up the matter with Bhumi Green Energy, the agency entrusted with biomining, once we receive a report on the judges’ visit. Thereafter, we will discuss other aspects, including how long it will take to cover the capped area,” said Mayor V.K. Minimol.

The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had earlier locked horns with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) over the supplementary agreement extending Bhumi Green Energy’s biomining contract without inviting fresh tenders. The agency is already engaged in the work. However, the UDF claimed that intense negotiations had helped bring down the biomining rate by ₹18 per tonne from the previously fixed ₹1,690, saving the Corporation around ₹60 lakh.

“Our position all along has been that there is no need to touch the already scientifically capped legacy waste. We have made it clear in the council as well. It will be an additional burden on the Corporation,” said V.A. Sreejith, LDF parliamentary party leader.

Former Mayor M. Anilkumar had, at a press conference in January, warned the UDF-led governing committee of the Kochi Corporation against overspending at Brahmapuram and overestimating the quantity of waste to be treated there, thereby paving the way for corruption. “Whatever more needs to be done should be done, but taxpayers’ money should not be wasted needlessly,” he had said, referring to the Mayor’s statement that Brahmapuram required new projects to improve its condition.

The Corporation had originally signed an agreement with Bhumi Green Energy on November 4, 2023, to biomine 7 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste within 16 months. The contract, initially scheduled to end on March 3, 2025, was later extended by eight months, until November 30, 2025.

articles.title: ‘Robust monitoring needed to ensure SC/ST sub-plan funds reach intended beneficiaries’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and Social Welfare Minister Adluri Laxman Kumar have directed officials to ensure effective utilisation of funds earmarked under the SC/ST Sub-Plan and to see that welfare and development benefits reach every eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) family in the State.

At a review meeting held at the Secretariat on Thursday, the Ministers stressed the need for a robust monitoring mechanism to ensure that Special Development Funds meant for the socio-economic advancement of SCs and STs are utilised strictly for their intended purpose, without any diversion.

Mr. Vikramarka instructed officials to comprehensively document the benefits accruing to SC and ST farmers through government programmes such as Rythu Bharosa, subsidised seed distribution and agricultural mechanisation initiatives. He also asked departments to explore alternative mechanisms wherever existing guidelines were hindering the optimal utilisation of Sub-Plan funds and to formulate proposals for targeted interventions that would provide greater support to eligible farmers from the two communities.

Mr. Laxman Kumar reiterated that funds allocated for SC and ST development should not be diverted under any circumstances. He called for continuous monitoring of department-wise expenditure, beneficiary coverage and the physical progress of works to ensure that every rupee spent under the Sub-Plan translated into tangible benefits for the intended communities.

Officials informed the meeting that district Collectors had identified around 1,300 acres of vacant government land across the State. Mr Bhatti asked departments to examine proposals for land acquisition wherever required to provide house sites to families without residential plots.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4.0% at its October policy meeting. The 12-member committee had a 10:2 voting pattern for maintaining the status quo, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal President Beth Hammack voted in favour of a 25 basis points hike.
The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.
While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.
“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

The stock market too traded lower in early trade but trimmed losses, with the Sensex trading 852.58 points higher to 74,098.61 at 2.30 p.m. The Nifty 50 was trading above 22,900. Analysts note that the Nifty must trade below 22,500 for bearishness to pertain.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market -- the Fed’s other mandate -- has been largely stable.
“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

articles.title: How neoliberalism turned the world against its young
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking

articles.title: Vedanta Group eyeing $20 billion profits over next two years: Chairman Anil Agarwal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Vedanta Group is targeting revenue of $50 billion and profits of $20 billion over the next two years, founder and chairman Anil Agarwal said at an industry event in Kolkata.
“This year we would be making $30 billion revenue and $11 billion in profits. In two years, we would scale our revenues to $50 billion with $20 billion in profits,” he said.
The privately-owned diversified commodities producer has interests spanning aluminium, zinc, oil and gas, power, iron and steel, copper and other critical minerals.

Separately, its recently listed Vedanta Aluminium reported more than a doubling of net profit year-on-year to ₹6,187 crore for the quarter ended September. Revenue rose 41% to ₹22,066 crore during the period.
The company increased aluminium production by 5% year-on-year to 649 kilotonnes (KT). Production of value-added aluminium products rose 31% to 432 KT, while alumina output climbed 37% to 895 KT.

Vedanta Aluminium also reduced its net debt by ₹3,090 crore during the quarter compared with the preceding quarter, signalling an improvement in its debt position alongside higher production and earnings.

articles.title: The way out of the dangerous trap
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India, celebrated as the world’s fastest-growing economy, has become the world’s fourth-largest economy, and is expected to be the next engine of global growth. Yet beneath these numbers lies a grim reality: India is drifting toward the middle-income trap, in which countries exhaust their gains from cheap labour and rapid catch-up and fail to transition to an innovation-driven, productivity-based economy. Weak job creation, stagnant wages, sluggish private investment, and low productivity are reinforcing one another, threatening to stall the country’s rise before it reaches high-income status. Many countries in the Global South are caught in this trap. India’s structural crisis is unique and more serious than not just a consequence of wars in West Asia disturbing its supply chain or premature automation from AI.

The signs of distress are visible in the youth protests across the country. Private investment remains sluggish, wage growth is stagnant, and household consumption is weak. Manufacturing has failed to generate enough jobs, while post-pandemic recovery has favoured large corporations and the digital economy, leaving the informal sector barely touched. Jobless growth emerges because productivity gains stay concentrated in narrow, capital- and skill-intensive enclaves that create little employment. This simultaneous rise of rising inequality and low productivity is a dangerous trap.

articles.title: Palestinian President says hopes for peace talks with new Israeli government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas said on Thursday (October 29, 2026) that he hoped the election of a new Israeli government would allow for the resumption of peace talks.

"For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace," Mr. Abbas said during a meeting with Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia.
"We hope that, immediately after a new Israeli government is formed, we will be able to engage in dialogue together," he added.

With almost all ballots counted from Israel's pivotal election, neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in parliament.
The uncertain outcome might mean weeks of trying to cobble together coalitions.
The Israeli-Palestinian peace process has been stalled for years, despite the recognition of the State of Palestine by a growing number of countries.
Under Mr. Netanyahu's watch, settlement construction and violence against Palestinians has soared in the occupied West Bank, where Mr. Abbas' Palestinian Authority exercises limited self-rule.

Ministers in Mr. Netanyahu's hard-right coalition have openly called for Israel's annexation of the West Bank and advocated policies encouraging Palestinians to leave the territory as well as the war-ravaged Gaza Strip.
Mr. Netanyahu led Israel in a devastating war which has left much of Gaza in rubble following Hamas's unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack.
Israel has since 1967 occupied the West Bank, where more than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements illegal under international law among some three million Palestinians.

articles.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc on Thursday (October 29, 2026) piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that could hold the key to forming a government after an inconclusive election.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation into allegations of fraud but cautioned against stigmatising the entire Arab Israeli community, who voted at unprecedented rates.

Israel was nearing the completion of ballot-counting from Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) election, in which neither Mr. Netanyahu nor the Opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in the parliament known as the Knesset.
The Netanyahu camp's accusations, which a key Arab party has rejected, could bring uncertainty to the electoral process at a time when the threat of a return to war with Iran looms over the region.

Israel's election saw soaring participation by Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the country's creation in 1948, as outrage boiled at calls by officials such as National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir to treat their community much as Israel has dealt with Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
Following Mr. Netanyahu's accusations of impropriety, Ben Gvir went so far as to encourage Israel to "immediately" order the arrests of Arab party leaders.
Raam party leader Mansour Abbas said he welcomed an investigation into claims of wrongdoing, adding that his moderate Islamist party had "no connection" with the accusations.

The Arab parties together have enough votes to take the opposition bloc over the finish line, but Mr. Eisenkot has baulked after relentless attacks by Mr. Netanyahu, who warned his right-wing Jewish base that voting for the Opposition would put Arabs in power.

Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, a conservative who heads the Central Election Commission, requested an investigation by the Shin Bet security service into allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas.
"The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel's elections have been stolen!" Mr. Netanyahu's Likud party said.
Government officials did not offer evidence to back the allegations, and left-wing candidate Yair Golan accused Mr. Netanyahu of attempting to stir controversy after failing to get a majority.
"Now he is trying to challenge the election results through an ugly delegitimisation campaign against the will of the people, and against the Arab public in particular."

articles.title: Israel election 2026: Benjamin Netanyahu is down but not out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israel’s October 27 election was framed by the Opposition as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu. For the country’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw the war on Gaza, attacked Iran twice and vowed not to make concessions to Palestinians, the election was a battle for survival. For the Opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, this was an opportunity to oust Mr. Netanyahu from power. With almost 90% of the vote counted, Israel is divided into three blocs, none of which can govern alone.

On the latest count, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has 53 seats, eight short of the 61 needed for a majority in the Knesset. His Likud is the largest party with 26 seats, down from 32 four years ago. His far-right partners, Otzma Yehudit of Ithamar Ben-Gvir (7) and Religious Zionism of Bezalel Smotrich (6), hold 13 between them, down slightly from 14 in the last election. The remaining seats in his bloc come from the religious parties—Shas and United Torah Judaism—each with seven seats.

articles.title: India ready to share battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners: Rajnath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: India is committed to collective regional security and the eradication of terrorism in all its forms and is ready to share its battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners to strengthen joint capabilities, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday (October 29, 2026).

Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines, Mr. Singh said India’s counter-terrorism experience was not theoretical knowledge but had been acquired through decades of confronting complex security challenges, including cross-border terrorism.
He said India’s strategies had been tested and refined through real-world operations, with Operation Sindoor demonstrating the country’s proactive counter-terrorism doctrine.
During the operation, India dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced a firm red line against state-sponsored terrorism, he said.

Emphasising that terrorism knows no borders, Mr. Singh said India was prepared to share its operational experience with ADMM-Plus partners through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes and intelligence sharing.
Counter-terrorism remains an important area of cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, with India and Malaysia co-chairing the Experts’ Working Group on Counter-Terrorism for the 2024-2027 cycle.

In a significant proposal to deepen regional engagement, Mr. Singh called for the establishment of a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ to strengthen institutional people-to-people connectivity between India and ASEAN countries. The ASEAN members appreciated the move of establishing ‘Youth Bridge’.

The initiative would promote digital innovation and capacity building, while providing greater opportunities for young people to contribute to regional peace and security. The proposal was appreciated by ASEAN members.

Highlighting the importance of maritime security, Mr. Singh said India had designated 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and had conducted the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He reiterated India’s commitment to freedom of navigation, international maritime law and the security of global sea lanes.

Pointing to the Indian Navy’s uninterrupted operational presence in the Gulf of Aden since 2008, he said India had escorted thousands of merchant vessels and thwarted dozens of hijacking attempts, irrespective of the vessels’ flag or nationality.

He reaffirmed India’s commitment to ASEAN centrality and a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, adding that New Delhi would continue to serve as a reliable net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and the wider Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: Bangladesh's tribunal sentences Awami League leader to death
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A special tribunal in Bangladesh on Thursday (October 29, 2026) sentenced Awami League's Joint General Secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death for the killing of six people during the July Uprising.
A three-member tribunal led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury and comprising Justices Md. Manjurul Bashid and Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir delivered the verdict.
"He will be hanged until death,” Mr. Chowdhury ruled after convicting him of killing six people in western Kushtia district during the 2024 violent student-led street protests.

The tribunal simultaneously sentenced to “imprisonment until death” three other Awami League leaders of the district unit on identical charges for their role in taming the protest dubbed the July Uprising that eventually toppled Sheikh Hasina’s government on August 5, 2024, when she fled to India.

All four accused, including Hanif, are absconding. The tribunal also ordered the confiscation of half of their property. Hanif is the 23rd leader of the now-disbanded Awami League to receive the capital punishment after the ouster of Sheikh Hasina.
They were all tried in absentia, with Sheikh Hasina being the first to be sentenced to death on November 17 last year, along with former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal.
Dozens more politicians and officials under the past government were sentenced to life imprisonment or other jail terms, while scores are facing trial in person or in absentia on different charges.

Ms. Hasina and her party leaders have called the tribunal a “kangaroo court” while international rights groups like Amnesty International, U.S.-based Human Rights Watch and prominent jurists questioned the fairness of the trials.
The ouster of the Awami League government installed an interim regime with Muhammad Yunus as its head. The tribunal's chief prosecutor Md. Aminul Islam welcomed the verdict, describing it as timely.

"The tribunal delivered its verdict today after completing the trial in this crimes against humanity case. Today's verdict is very timely. Paying tribute to the July martyrs, we welcome the verdict," he said. The convicts were defended by state-appointed lawyers.

articles.title: Albania opposition disrupts parliament session after violent street protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Opposition lawmakers in Albania disrupted a parliament session by letting off flares on Thursday (October 29, 2026) ​following weeks of violent anti-government protests called by students ‌demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.
Members ​of the Opposition Democratic Party of ⁠Albania also blocked access to the podium when a law on the Central Bank was being voted on.

"These (ruling lawmakers) are ‌criminals and they deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls and broken bones, not the ‌young people," Opposition leader Sali Berisha said ‌during his ⁠speech before his microphone was cut off.
Other ⁠Opposition members surrounded him during the speech, holding photos of protesters injured by rubber bullets. Some held aloft blue flares, the ​colour of their ‌party.

Student-led demonstrations, fuelled by anger over perceived government corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards, have engulfed central Tirana since mid-October and spread to ‌other cities.
Demonstrators demanding Mr. Rama's resignation have set ​fire to government buildings and banks, smashed shop windows and pulled up paving stones to ⁠throw at police.

The unrest, which followed months of largely peaceful summer protests against a luxury coastal development ‌backed by U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, poses the biggest challenge yet to Mr. Rama, who has governed since 2013 and won a fourth term in office last year.

On Sunday (October 25, 2026), Mr. Rama introduced new measures to curb violence, including fines of 500,000 ‌lek ($6,200) for anyone who participates in a protest that turns ​violent, even if they do not personally commit acts of violence.
This week the protests ⁠were mainly peaceful, and another is planned for Saturday (October 31, 2026).

Prime Minister ⁠Rama has again called on students for dialogue and introduced new economic measures such ‌as cheaper fuel and more money for poor families in an attempt to stop the violence in ​the streets.

articles.title: Experts warn of wider spread as Ebola outbreak reaches plateau
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Ebola outbreak in Congo passed a grim milestone this week — 10,000 confirmed cases — and spurred questions about whether health authorities are losing their ability to contain it.

Nearly half the infected people in this outbreak have died, and some experts say there are reasons to worry this could grow into the worst Ebola outbreak in history. Others don't think it will reach that level. Researchers are currently working on updated projections.

Current circumstances suggest it's unlikely to spark significant problems in most other countries, some researchers said. But about 30 confirmed cases have already popped up in other nations. And the risk that more will appear outside Congo will grow if the outbreak isn't tamed, said Justin Lessler, a University of North Carolina researcher who studies the dynamics of infectious disease outbreaks.
Experts also are hopeful that a vaccine will become available next year that could help control it.

At a virtual summit of African health ministers on Wednesday, Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya said the continent is “not winning” the fight against Ebola and needs to do more after it spread to multiple African countries. “Together, we agreed to prepare every country, coordinate across our borders and keep those borders open while watching them closely,” Kaseya wrote on X.
Steady case numbers raise concerns about spread beyond Congo

About 400 to 500 new confirmed cases have been reported in Congo each week, and that number seems to be holding steady. It's good news that “cases are not rising exponentially,” at least for the moment, said Dr. Boghuma Titanji, an Emory University infectious disease specialist.
“But they're not coming down, either," she said. "It's at a plateau. And the plateau is at a very, very high set point."

A major challenge in Congo is limited contact tracing and collaboration with affected communities; health workers sometimes spend more time trying to convince locals to work with them than giving care.

Fewer than a quarter of new cases are coming from people known to have been in contact with an infected person, showing there are ongoing chains of transmission that health authorities are not aware of.

As cases mount, the likelihood grows that more infected people travel to other countries, Titanji and other experts said. France, Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda also have reported cases tied to the Congo outbreak.

Travel restrictions, like those imposed by the US, can make it harder for the virus to leave Africa. And in many places where a traveller's infection may surface, health officials should be able to quickly isolate an infected person and find any contacts, experts say.

articles.title: ICMR funds study to identify genetic links, potential therapies for autoimmune diseases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Indian Council of Medical Research has funded a four-year study to investigate the genetic and immunological mechanisms underlying autoimmune diseases by studying families with multiple affected members, AIIMS doctors said on Thursday, appealing to SLE patients to get enrolled in the study.

The project titled ‘Genomic Profiling and Identification of Targetable Shared Immunopathogenic Events in Multiplex Families with Autoimmune Diseases’ has been awarded to Dipyaman Ganguly of Ashoka University, Sonipat, Haryana, and Ranjan Gupta, additional professor in the Department of Rheumatology, AIIMS, Delhi.

The study aims to build a nationwide cohort of 200 families in which multiple members are affected by autoimmune diseases. Each participating family must have at least one member diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), commonly known as lupus, Gupta said.

The researchers will conduct genetic and immunological assessments of the enrolled patients and their family members to identify shared biological mechanisms that contribute to the development of these conditions.
The findings could help scientists better understand the disease processes involved and identify potential targets for developing new therapies, he said.

Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues. A family history of such conditions is associated with an increased risk of developing them, highlighting the importance of investigating genetic and shared immunological factors, Gupta said.

The four-year project will involve clinical centres at AIIMS Delhi; AIIMS Bibinagar, Telangana; Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGIMS), Lucknow; St John's Hospital, Bengaluru; Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad; and the Kolkata Medical College. These centres will contribute clinical data and biological samples for the study.
Patients diagnosed with lupus and residing in Delhi-NCR can contact the centre at AIIMS Delhi to check their eligibility for participation, Gupta said.
Participation will be subject to eligibility assessment and the study's enrolment requirements.

articles.title: Heat-related deaths up 36% since Paris Agreement as climate action lags: Lancet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Some of the health harms of climate change grew faster in the decade since the Paris Agreement entered into force (2016-2025) than in the previous decade (2006-2015) as climate action fails to keep pace, according to the 10th Lancet Countdown Report on Health and Climate Change .
The report, which was released on Wednesday, said the annual average heat-related deaths rose by nearly 36% globally after the Paris Agreement was introduced.
"In 2023 alone, heat was linked to a record 710,000 deaths with more than 70 per cent of that toll attributable to human-caused climate change," it said.

The analysis represents the work of 146 multidisciplinary researchers from more than 100 institutions across more than 30 countries. It tracks 54 indicators of the health impacts of climate change and the health effects of climate action.

The report highlights that cleaner energy, more resilient health systems, more health-protecting legislation and growing scientific evidence have brought real health benefits to local communities since the Paris Agreement, but these gains are still too slow, too insufficient, and too inconsistent to offset the growing risks.
"Rising overall energy demand and slow system change means fossil fuels still supply over 80% of the world's energy, and climate-heating emissions reached a record high in 2024," it said.
The report added that despite gains in some countries, fossil-fuel air pollution still kills an estimated 2.8 million people a year worldwide.
Moreover, adaptation funding is falling far short of what's needed.

According to the report, the health adaptation needs quantified so far by developing countries put the minimum cost at $3.3 billion a year, based on data from only 48 of the 79 countries that have completed these estimates.
However, only around a third of this declared need, $1.1 billion, was committed in 2024.

"This substantial financing gap is reflected in countries' ability to translate adaptation priorities into action, with finance and human resourcing identified as the top barriers to implementation of Health National Adaptation Plans," said the report.

articles.title: Why ongoing symptoms and patients’ lived experiences need more attention in lupus care
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: When Nisha Panwar,30, was diagnosed with lupus in December 2013, she felt relieved. After months of recurrent fever, rashes and worsening symptoms, she finally had an explanation for what was happening to her body. Before the diagnosis, she says, several doctors had told her she had no disease and that it was “all in my head” and was referred to a psychiatrist.

For Tabassum Sultana, 28, a Bengaluru-based content creator, the diagnosis of mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), with features of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), in 2024 was followed by another setback. She developed avascular necrosis of the right hip and underwent surgery in September 2025. Her recovery was slow, she became dependent on her mother for everyday activities and had to stop working. Recurring flare-ups continue to affect her mental health.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

fullParagraphs: Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods.

The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. The Court has also upbraided local authorities for failing to enforce pollution norms by citing the Court’s own stay of a 2022 National Green Tribunal order imposing a compensation on the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation and the local administration in Jodhpur and Barmer. The State regulatory apparatus has been dysfunctional: officials were aware of illegal mining operations in some areas, yet they regularised leases in those areas. Given the dereliction in play, the Court is correct to treat the possibility of collusion between State officials and industrial mafias seriously. Justice Mehta’s observation that the State could be held liable under the ‘polluter pays’ principle is also a significant indictment of state failure, through negligence. Now, importantly, the State still has to restore the Jojari and attend to its wellbeing, which is relevant to a recent tendency by the Court to substitute itself for regulators rather than disciplining them into discharging their functions. This needs to change.

articles.title: Dubious retreat: On the National Medical Commission and its MSMER
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has denotified and withdrawn its 2023 Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations (MSMER ), diminishing the framework of penalties vis-à-vis educational standards and infrastructure at medical colleges. The move is noteworthy as the MSMER provided for fines of up to ₹5 lakh on faculty members and administrators for submitting false information. Fortunately, the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) retains the power to fine errant institutions up to ₹1 crore under the 2023 Establishment of Medical Institutions, Assessment and Rating Regulations . MSMER was lauded for its intention to crack down on the deep-seated corruption and malpractice in medical colleges, particularly over ‘ghost faculty’ and ‘ghost patients’. The NMC’s justification is that MSMER also introduced a parallel mechanism allowing undergraduate and postgraduate boards to evaluate institutions, stepping on the MARB’s toes. However, why the NMC scrapped MSMER wholesale is unclear. The 2023 Postgraduate Medical Education Regulations remain in force and include a provision to fine individual faculty members at postgraduate medical colleges. Non-compliance among medical colleges is not uncommon and seldom nipped in the bud, even as the number of medical seats swells while the transparency of the medical education system has not improved.

Notwithstanding the provision to fine individuals at postgraduate centres, the MARB and the NMC can only penalise institutions, which is harder and risks creating a perverse incentive to accommodate rather than punish, and could mitigate the fear that keeps administrators honest. MSMER also specified timelines to appeal penalties. Although the MARB regulations retain the appeal processes, their 15-day deadline could conflict with the 60-day period under the NMC Act, potentially creating legal disputes that delay penal action. There is also a telling incident. As part of a proceeding under the RTI Act, the Central Information Commission revealed last year that the NMC had stated in 2024 that MARB had neither formally assessed nor rated medical colleges and that its standard forms need not be made public. In a revised reply in October 2025, it said the responding NMC officer’s records did not include any of the corresponding reports. However, the 2023 MARB regulations require the Board to publish its latest annual assessment results. If the NMC withdrew MSMER because the powers thereunder also exist elsewhere, the public deserves to know whether the powers are also being exercised and whether the outcomes are as publicly accessible as intended. Unless the NMC has satisfactory answers for all these lacunae, the withdrawal will appear less like simplification and more like regulatory relaxation.

articles.title: A final surge: On Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s triumph in Brazil
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: At one point, it seemed almost impossible for Brazil’s 80-year-old President, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, to turn the tide after finishing second to Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of elections on October 4. In Brazil’s history, no candidate who has finished second in the first round has gone on to win the presidential run-off. Most of the candidates who dropped out after the first round were from the right. Flávio’s Liberal Party cemented its position in both houses of Congress, while right-wing candidates won several provincial elections. But Lula, a former trade unionist and organiser, who lost a finger in an accident as a teenager, was not ready to give up. Lula and his Workers’ Party identified campaign weaknesses, shifted their attention to economic issues, promised growth and welfare, and persuaded more voters to turn out for Sunday’s run-off. Lula won 51.7% of the vote against Flávio’s 48.2%, a greater lead than his victory against Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, four years ago. Over the weeks, Lula turned the right-wing’s gains in the first round against it, highlighting the threats that a Bolsonaro victory could pose to democracy and civil rights. Flávio’s campaign pledge to free his father — he is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting to overturn Lula’s 2022 victory, and impeach Supreme Court judges — only heightened the concerns of voters outside the right wing, who rallied behind a familiar face.

Lula unleashed a social media campaign to mobilise younger voters. A WhatsApp channel called ‘Lula’s Army’ with 11 million followers spread his message of continuity. He also announced plans to expand a cash payout scheme for the poor, a new debt relief package and entrepreneur-friendly measures. In the northeast, the Workers’ Party’s stronghold, he gained nearly three million votes and made considerable gains in the working-class neighbourhoods of big cities, including São Paulo. A relatively stable economic record, marked by growth and falling unemployment over the past three and a half years, also lent credibility to Lula’s appeal. His victory bucks the recent trend in South America, where Washington-aligned right-wing and conservative forces have gained ground. While Lula offers predictable stability and social and economic inclusiveness, he could also be, as the President of South America’s largest economy, a voice of resistance to Donald Trump’s imperial ambitions. At the same time, Lula will have to work with a right-wing-controlled Congress to advance his agenda. He should seek to build legislative consensus while focusing on addressing the economic challenges of Brazil, which remains one of the most unequal major world economies.

articles.title: Food Safety officials conduct State-wide inspection at 45 packaged drinking water units; notices issued to 24
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Food Safety and Drug Administration Department conducted a special State-wide inspection of 45 packaged drinking water units on Thursday.

Several violations, including unhygienic conditions, absence of medical fitness certificates for staff, missing licences from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), labelling defects and failure to produce pest control certificates, were found during the inspection.
As many as 32 water samples have been sent to government food laboratories for testing, while notices have been issued to 24 units for the violations.
Officials of the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department during a special State-wide inspection at packaged drinking water units on Thursday. | Photo Credit: SUDHAKARA JAIN
Misbranded packaged drinking water was seized from units in Mysuru and Davangere. A unit at Mulbagal in Kolar district was shut down due to unhygienic conditions.
Health Minister U.T. Khader has advised consumers to verify the FSSAI licence number, ISI mark, manufacturing date and integrity of the seal before purchasing packaged drinking water.
He also urged the public to report irregularities by scanning the QR code provided for lodging complaints.

articles.title: Three missing fishermen rescued
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Three fishermen from Chollangipeta in Tallarevu mandal in Kakinada district, who went missing after their boat capsized at sea on Tuesday, were rescued by rescue teams.
After their boat capsized, the three managed to swim to Hope Island where they got stranded among the vegetation.
Upon receiving information about the incident, the Fisheries Department, the Real-Time Governance Society (RTGS), and disaster management agencies immediately launched a search and rescue operation.
Using 10 boats, the teams located the fishermen on Thursday and brought them safely back to the shore.

Officials said that such incidents occur when warnings issued to avoid venturing out to sea for fishing due severe weather conditions are ignored. Officials urged fishermen to strictly follow government warnings for their own safety.

articles.title: Power sector suffers ₹500-crore damage due to Cyclone Arnab, says Minister

articles.title: Fishing boat catches fire near Feroke
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A fishing boat docked beneath the old Feroke bridge caught fire early on Thursday (October 29, 2026) morning, triggering safety concerns among residents. The incident, which occurred when workers were away from the spot, reportedly originated in the boat’s engine and fuel tank.

According to the initial assessment by rescue squads, the blaze broke out in the engine section before spreading to other parts rapidly. Prompt response from emergency personnel helped avert a major disaster. Two officers waded into the river with ropes, swam to the boat, secured it safely, and assisted teams in pulling the vessel closer to the bank.

Fire and rescue services personnel subsequently pumped water to fully extinguish the flames. A rescue officer said a technical malfunction in the boat’s engine caused the fire. He added that further investigations were on to determine the exact cause of the fire.

articles.title: Court directive to add to Kochi Corporation’s Brahmapuram biomining costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kochi Corporation will have to biomine an additional 1.26 lakh tonnes of scientifically capped legacy waste, further adding to its financial burden.

This follows a direction issued by Kerala High Court judges P. Gopinath and Bechu Kurian Thomas during a visit to the Brahmapuram waste treatment plant last month, asking the civic body to include the scientifically capped legacy waste in the biomining process as well. The High Court has been closely monitoring activities at Brahmapuram since a major fire broke out in heaps of plastic waste in 2023 and continued for nearly a fortnight.

Earlier this year, the National Institute of Technology-Calicut (NIT-C) submitted a report to the Corporation estimating the total remaining legacy waste at 3.22 lakh metric tonnes, including the scientifically capped waste. The Corporation had decided not to disturb the capped waste and instead carry out biomining of the remaining 1.96 lakh tonnes at a negotiated rate of ₹1,672 per metric tonne, amounting to ₹37 crore. However, the cost may now have to be recalculated following the directive to include the capped waste as well.

“We will take up the matter with Bhumi Green Energy, the agency entrusted with biomining, once we receive a report on the judges’ visit. Thereafter, we will discuss other aspects, including how long it will take to cover the capped area,” said Mayor V.K. Minimol.

The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had earlier locked horns with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) over the supplementary agreement extending Bhumi Green Energy’s biomining contract without inviting fresh tenders. The agency is already engaged in the work. However, the UDF claimed that intense negotiations had helped bring down the biomining rate by ₹18 per tonne from the previously fixed ₹1,690, saving the Corporation around ₹60 lakh.

“Our position all along has been that there is no need to touch the already scientifically capped legacy waste. We have made it clear in the council as well. It will be an additional burden on the Corporation,” said V.A. Sreejith, LDF parliamentary party leader.

Former Mayor M. Anilkumar had, at a press conference in January, warned the UDF-led governing committee of the Kochi Corporation against overspending at Brahmapuram and overestimating the quantity of waste to be treated there, thereby paving the way for corruption. “Whatever more needs to be done should be done, but taxpayers’ money should not be wasted needlessly,” he had said, referring to the Mayor’s statement that Brahmapuram required new projects to improve its condition.

The Corporation had originally signed an agreement with Bhumi Green Energy on November 4, 2023, to biomine 7 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste within 16 months. The contract, initially scheduled to end on March 3, 2025, was later extended by eight months, until November 30, 2025.

articles.title: ‘Robust monitoring needed to ensure SC/ST sub-plan funds reach intended beneficiaries’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and Social Welfare Minister Adluri Laxman Kumar have directed officials to ensure effective utilisation of funds earmarked under the SC/ST Sub-Plan and to see that welfare and development benefits reach every eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) family in the State.

At a review meeting held at the Secretariat on Thursday, the Ministers stressed the need for a robust monitoring mechanism to ensure that Special Development Funds meant for the socio-economic advancement of SCs and STs are utilised strictly for their intended purpose, without any diversion.

Mr. Vikramarka instructed officials to comprehensively document the benefits accruing to SC and ST farmers through government programmes such as Rythu Bharosa, subsidised seed distribution and agricultural mechanisation initiatives. He also asked departments to explore alternative mechanisms wherever existing guidelines were hindering the optimal utilisation of Sub-Plan funds and to formulate proposals for targeted interventions that would provide greater support to eligible farmers from the two communities.

Mr. Laxman Kumar reiterated that funds allocated for SC and ST development should not be diverted under any circumstances. He called for continuous monitoring of department-wise expenditure, beneficiary coverage and the physical progress of works to ensure that every rupee spent under the Sub-Plan translated into tangible benefits for the intended communities.

Officials informed the meeting that district Collectors had identified around 1,300 acres of vacant government land across the State. Mr Bhatti asked departments to examine proposals for land acquisition wherever required to provide house sites to families without residential plots.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4.0% at its October policy meeting. The 12-member committee had a 10:2 voting pattern for maintaining the status quo, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal President Beth Hammack voted in favour of a 25 basis points hike.
The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.
While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.
“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

The stock market too traded lower in early trade but trimmed losses, with the Sensex trading 852.58 points higher to 74,098.61 at 2.30 p.m. The Nifty 50 was trading above 22,900. Analysts note that the Nifty must trade below 22,500 for bearishness to pertain.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market -- the Fed’s other mandate -- has been largely stable.
“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

fullParagraphs: Vedanta Group is targeting revenue of $50 billion and profits of $20 billion over the next two years, founder and chairman Anil Agarwal said at an industry event in Kolkata.
“This year we would be making $30 billion revenue and $11 billion in profits. In two years, we would scale our revenues to $50 billion with $20 billion in profits,” he said.
The privately-owned diversified commodities producer has interests spanning aluminium, zinc, oil and gas, power, iron and steel, copper and other critical minerals.

Separately, its recently listed Vedanta Aluminium reported more than a doubling of net profit year-on-year to ₹6,187 crore for the quarter ended September. Revenue rose 41% to ₹22,066 crore during the period.
The company increased aluminium production by 5% year-on-year to 649 kilotonnes (KT). Production of value-added aluminium products rose 31% to 432 KT, while alumina output climbed 37% to 895 KT.

Vedanta Aluminium also reduced its net debt by ₹3,090 crore during the quarter compared with the preceding quarter, signalling an improvement in its debt position alongside higher production and earnings.

fullParagraphs: India, celebrated as the world’s fastest-growing economy, has become the world’s fourth-largest economy, and is expected to be the next engine of global growth. Yet beneath these numbers lies a grim reality: India is drifting toward the middle-income trap, in which countries exhaust their gains from cheap labour and rapid catch-up and fail to transition to an innovation-driven, productivity-based economy. Weak job creation, stagnant wages, sluggish private investment, and low productivity are reinforcing one another, threatening to stall the country’s rise before it reaches high-income status. Many countries in the Global South are caught in this trap. India’s structural crisis is unique and more serious than not just a consequence of wars in West Asia disturbing its supply chain or premature automation from AI.

The signs of distress are visible in the youth protests across the country. Private investment remains sluggish, wage growth is stagnant, and household consumption is weak. Manufacturing has failed to generate enough jobs, while post-pandemic recovery has favoured large corporations and the digital economy, leaving the informal sector barely touched. Jobless growth emerges because productivity gains stay concentrated in narrow, capital- and skill-intensive enclaves that create little employment. This simultaneous rise of rising inequality and low productivity is a dangerous trap.
